findings: Fit: the section reuses the take-apart stack as specified. The import map has the same two entries as src/take-apart-page.js, the routes are the existing /vendor/* and /models/patch-one.glb, /take-apart-model.js supplies the model, and no vendored copy is added. The new routes in src/index.js (/home-layers.js, /img/home-layers.webp) follow the dynamic-import and text()/webp() helper pattern of the neighbouring routes.

Layering: src/page.js only imports home-layered.js and inserts the section between #patch and #how. The client and image bytes live in separate lazily imported modules. src/images.js and the four existing image routes are untouched.

Bundling: the client is a literal string with no function.toString and a static dynamic-import path, consistent with the take-apart bundling decision. The gate is small and inline. The home document grows by 3,603 B and the lazy payload is 1,209,685 B (GLB counted once), both inside budget.
Not blocking: brain/decisions does not exist in the repo, so I judged fit against brain/project.md, the spec and the take-apart code. No decision record was available to contradict.

Minor: the home client duplicates scene setup (camera, lights, material fade, framing) from take-apart-client.js instead of sharing it. This is acceptable because the take-apart page must stay untouched, but it risks drift.
Minor: the onward link href is /take-apart?from=home, not plain /take-apart as in R7. It resolves to the same page.

Process, for the approving station: the working tree edits .openspec/specs/home-layered-view/spec.md (R8, R9, R11, S6), so the approver should confirm those amendments were authorised. The suite shows 3 failures (design v4 S11 plus two product-model S7/R13 tests), not the single S11 failure the work order allows. The two extra failures predate this change but must be itemized by name in the run report, as reviewer-spec already noted. My review output is saved at runs/wo-gh-13/reviewer-architecture.output.md.
